40001.name: Bhogawati
40001.why: Wikipedia: rises on the Balaghat scarp near Dharashiv (Osmanabad), flows ~65 km SW through Barshi and Madha talukas and joins the Sina near Mohol - matches source, course, length and mouth. CWC's three 'Bhogavati/Bhogawati' lines are different rivers (Kolhapur, Tapi and Godavari basins). Catchment 1,647 km2 - the largest humid-zone gap found.

40025.name: Oshiwara
40025.why: Mumbai river from the Aarey hills to Malad Creek, absent from CWC. Course from the OpenStreetMap "Oshiwara River" ways, ending where it meets the Malad Creek channel (drawn by CWC as the lower Poisar, uid 9009).

40026.name: Vakola Nala
40026.why: Rises north of Santacruz East and joins the Mithi (CWC "Mahim") just above Mahim Creek. OSM names it "Vakola Nala" (water area 39749207); the line follows the unnamed OSM waterways along it.

40027.name: Mahul Creek
40027.why: From the Ghatkopar West hills through Vidyavihar, Shell Colony and Kurla East, then south past Chunabhatti and Wadala along Mahul Road into Mumbai Harbour; the stretch past Antop Hill is the Mumbai City / Suburban district boundary. Unnamed in OSM; "Mahul Creek" is the name of its tidal outlet.

40028.why: Unnamed. Rises in the Ghatkopar hills near R City Mall, runs through Ghatkopar East and along the north edge of the Deonar dumping ground into Thane Creek. Unnamed OSM waterways.

40029.name: Desai Khadi (north branch)
40029.why: Northern headstream of the Desai Khadi, from the hills south of Ambernath to the junction by the Taloja Bypass.

40030.name: Desai Khadi (south branch)
40030.why: Southern headstream of the Desai Khadi, from the hills south of Ambernath to the junction by the Taloja Bypass.

40031.name: Desai Khadi
40031.why: Formed by its two branches by the Taloja Bypass, flows west past Nilaje and Desai village, south of Diva, and north into the Ulhas near Mumbra. OSM way 204366002 and neighbours (unnamed); Desai village sits on its bank.

40032.name: Chena
40032.why: OSM "Chena River": from the Yeoor hills of Sanjay Gandhi National Park north to the Ulhas (Vasai Creek) at Ghodbunder.

40033.name: Waldhuni
40033.why: OSM "Waldhuni River" and "Wadhuni": from near Ambernath through Ulhasnagar to the Ulhas at Shahad, Kalyan. OSM maps only its lower course.

40034.name: Irla Nala
40034.why: OSM "Irla Nala": from Vile Parle west through Irla to the sea at Juhu.

40035.name: Mogara Nallah
40035.why: OSM "Mogara Nallah": through Andheri West to Malad Creek near Lokhandwala.

40036.name: Chandansar
40036.why: Unmapped in OSM; HydroRIVERS course from the hills east of the Jivdani temple, Virar, north past Chandansar village (on Chandansar Road) to the Vaitarna. Name as the user gave it.

40037.name: Somaiyya Nalla
40037.why: OSM "Somaiyya Nalla": rises at Tilak Nagar, about 1 km from Lokmanya Tilak Terminus, runs east under the Eastern Express Highway, along the Ghatkopar-Mankhurd Link Road and east to the unnamed river at the north-west corner of the Deonar dumping ground; their joint channel reaches Thane Creek.

40038.why: The overflow from Powai Lake into the Mithi: OSM drain from the lake shore north of the Powai Dam to the river near Saki Vihar Road. Unnamed in OSM.

40039.name: Kukatpally Nala
40039.why: Musi tributary from Fox Sagar's outlet south past Jeedimetla, Qutubullapur and Balanagar, under the west end of Begumpet Airport, into Hussain Sagar from the north (HMDA names the Kukatpally Nala as the lake's northern feeder, with a catchment over Jeedimetla, Qutbullapur and Balanagar). OSM ways; the line crosses the lake to its outlet.

40040.name: Hussain Sagar Surplus Nala
40040.why: Hussain Sagar's outflow, past Gandhi Nagar and Ashok Nagar and north of Kacheguda station, to the Musi south-east of Kacheguda. OSM "Ashoknagar Nala".

40041.name: Picket Nala
40041.why: Hussain Sagar's north-eastern feeder (HMDA): from north-west of Old Alwal pond through Bon Cheruvu, under the east end of Begumpet Airport, into the lake between Sanjeevaiah Park and James Street. HydroRIVERS reach 41256718 to Bon Cheruvu (no OSM waterway there), then OSM ways; the line crosses the lake to its outlet.

40042.why: From the tank near Jagadgirigutta (probably Pariki Cheruvu, unnamed in OSM) south through Kukatpally and Bharath Nagar to the Kukatpally Nala at Balanagar, north of Begumpet Airport. OSM ways, unnamed.

40043.why: Through Mullakathuva, Kamuni and Chinna Maisamma Cheruvus to the stream from Jagadgirigutta at Bharath Nagar, north of Sanathnagar station. HydroRIVERS reach 41256945; OSM maps only short stubs here.

40044.name: Koramangala Valley (K-100)
40044.why: BBMP storm-water drain K-100, the Koramangala valley's main channel, from Majestic through Koramangala to Bellandur Lake. OSM ways tagged K100; the line crosses the lake to its outlet.

40045.name: Challaghatta Valley (C-100)
40045.why: BBMP storm-water drain C-100, the Challaghatta valley's main channel, from central Bengaluru past Domlur and Challaghatta to Bellandur Lake. OSM ways tagged C100; the line crosses the lake to its outlet.

40046.why: The Koramangala-Challaghatta valley below Bellandur Lake: Bellandur overflows to Varthur Lake, which drains down the plateau to the Dakshina Pinakini. Unnamed OSM waterways.

40047.name: Hebbal Valley (H-200)
40047.why: BBMP storm-water drain H-200, the Hebbal valley's main channel, through Hebbal and Nagavara lakes; Nagavara's outflow joins H-300. OSM ways tagged H200 and unnamed ways below Nagavara.

40048.name: Hebbal Valley (H-300)
40048.why: BBMP storm-water drain H-300 in the Hebbal valley, from east of the city centre north-east towards Kalkere. OSM ways tagged H300.

40049.why: The Hebbal valley from the end of H-300 to Yellamallappa Chetty Lake (Medahalli). Unnamed OSM waterways; the line crosses the lake to its outlet.

40050.name: Hebbal Valley (BD-423)
40050.why: BBMP storm-water drain BD-423: the Yellamallappa Chetty Lake outflow to the Dakshina Pinakini. OSM ways tagged BD423.

40051.name: Nagarbhavi Thorai
40051.why: The western branch of the Vrishabhavati, from Peenya past Laggere and Nagarbhavi to the confluence near Bangalore University. CWC drew it as the head of the Vrishabhavati; OSM and the Paani.Earth basin map name it the Nagarbhavi. OSM ways "Nagarbhavi Thorai" and "Nagarbhavi Drain".
